newsitem.title: UK: Higher oil price fuels BP profit.
newsitem.headline: Higher oil price fuels BP profit.

text.p: British Petroleum Tuesday reported a 30 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 2.62 billion pounds ($4.28 billion), thanks to productivity gains and strong oil prices.
The result excludes a fourth quarter exceptional charge of 341 million pounds ($557 million), covering one-time costs related to the merger of BP and Mobil Corp's downstream operations in Europe.

The company said productivity improvements through volume growth, higher value sales and cost reductions produced gains of around $600 million, generating most of the year-on-year improvement in underlying profit.
Although oil prices were higher, particularly during the second half of the year, BP said this was partly offset by lower chemical margins.

The company said continuing strong demand, relatively modest production increases and the decision by the Organisation of Oil Producing Countries (OPEC) in December to roll over its production quotas enabled the oil market to absorb the initial resumption in oil exports from Iraq.
BP said an increase in the rate of production growth over the coming months might subject oil prices to renewed volatility.
The company said it expects its own oil production to increase further this year, while pressure on refined oil products margins may moderate if the crude oil price weakens during the year.

In chemicals, healthy demand should keep prices steady, but profit margins might continue to be affected by high oil-related feedstock prices. Results will remain sensitive to the strength of the British pound, BP said.

Net profits before exceptional items rose by 27 percent in the fourth quarter to 689 million pounds ($1.1 billion), and the company raised its quarterly dividend by five percent over the previous quarter to 5.25 pence (8-1/2 cents).
